name: Medullary Cystic Kidney Disease
aliases: Nephronophthisis Medullary Cystic Kidney Disease Complex

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Medullary Cystic Kidney Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of autosomal dominant family history of progressive renal disease
Identification of cysts localized to the renal medulla on imaging studies
Evidence of progressive chronic kidney disease leading to end-stage renal failure
Kidneys are typically normal sized or small, distinguishing from polycystic kidney disease
Histological evidence of tubulointerstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy on biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of autosomal dominant family history, medullary cysts on imaging, and progressive renal failure
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for mutations in MUC1 or UMOD genes can support diagnosis

pathognomonic.notes: Cysts localized specifically to the renal medulla

pathognomonic.symptomName: Polyuria and nocturia due to impaired concentrating ability

common.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic kidney disease

common.notes: Due to impaired renal tubular function

rare.symptomName: Renal cyst infection or abscess formation

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen indicating renal failure
Electrolyte abnormalities such as hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing multiple small cysts confined to the renal medulla
Normal or small kidney size without cortical cysts
other: Renal biopsy showing tubulointerstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy

distinguishingFeatures: Enlarged kidneys with cysts throughout cortex and medulla
Hypertension and hematuria more common early
Mutations in PKD1 or PKD2 genes
Medullary cysts with more prominent tubular basement membrane disruption

redFlags: Rapid progression to end-stage renal disease
Family history of early-onset renal failure
Severe electrolyte disturbances refractory to treatment
references: Hildebrandt F, et al. Medullary cystic kidney disease: clinical and molecular aspects. Kidney Int. 2017.
Olinger E, et al. Genetic basis of medullary cystic kidney disease. Nat Rev Nephrol. 2019.
